items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — opened 'Hi, this is Jules. How can I help you today?' and went straight into data collection with no roadmap or timeframe. Also never asked 'how are you today?' — 'how can I help you' is not the warm-up.

No booking attempt at all — the single biggest miss. Jules had confirmed live availability ('we're fully available on the eighth'), quoted a price, answered the deposit question, and then closed with 'when you're ready to get this scheduled feel free to give us a call back.' He never once asked for the date. A quote-ready, availability-confirmed, no-objection caller was handed back to herself.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — on a move with a 75-inch TV, two recliners, and a third-floor stairs-only carry-down. The customer even pre-empted damage risk herself ('it'll be protected') and got no coverage pitch in response.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.

Packing services never offered or priced, despite the customer saying outright 'I still have a lot of craft to pack.' That is an explicit buying signal for packing revenue and it was answered with 'No problem at all.'

Box count never nailed down and the customer's direct question was never answered. She asked for help: 'I don't know an estimate on boxes... everybody's telling me average for a one bedroom is twenty to thirty boxes. And I feel like I already have thirty boxes filled up.' Jules replied 'No problem at all' and moved on — so the estimate was built with an unknown, and growing, box count.
No Ecobox referral on a caller who volunteered that she needs more boxes and is still actively packing — a textbook relevant referral, skipped.

Estimate is very likely understated. 2.5–4 hours with two movers for a one-bedroom load (queen bed, twin bunk, two recliners, dresser, bookshelf, desk, 75-inch TV, 30+ boxes with more coming) carried down three flights with no elevator, driven from 75126 to Garland, then up to a third floor. The 2.5-hour minimum was presented as a realistic floor on a job that cannot physically hit it.

Drive time / trip fee never addressed. Origin zip 75126 (Forney) to Garland is a real leg of the day and it never appeared in the estimate or the pricing, and no trip-fee applicability was checked out loud.

Stairs were collected but never priced into the range out loud. The only nod was the vague 'just really depends on the access from the apartments.' He learned it was third-floor stairs-only and the quoted range did not visibly change.
Walk distance and special considerations (long walks, narrow stairwells, tight turns, loading-zone parking at the complex) never probed — the highest-variance factors on a third-floor apartment move.
Never asked about additional stops — notable, because the customer volunteered that her twenty-year-old son 'is moving out on his own,' which is an obvious second-stop or split-load scenario.
Never asked about storage, garage/balcony/storage-closet items, or moving stressors ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').

Save Your Ass prep speech essentially absent. The only prep line was reactive — 'if everything's already disassembled and we'll make the move a whole lot quicker' — after the customer told him she was breaking down the beds herself 'trying to save on time.' No consolidation examples (loose drawer items, photos off walls, kids'/craft supplies boxed), no 'take a carload' tip, no close on it. She handed him the coaching moment and he took the credit instead of the sale.

Clock start never explained — no 'the clock starts on-site when we open the contract.' The 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorating, and 'does that make sense so far?' were all covered well, but the customer does not know when the meter starts.

Destination address was never resolved and the destination zip was never captured. Customer gave '5620 prosperity drive in Garland,' it would not pull up, Jules said 'I can just use the zip code' — and then never asked for it. The exact address failure that caused this inbound call was left unfixed in the record.

Email address never read back for confirmation. She said 'JM Dody 01 @gmail.com' on a line where her last name had already been misheard twice, and Jules answered 'Got it.' Every deliverable on this call rides on that address being right.

Website address-lookup bug never escalated or acknowledged as a defect. The customer diagnosed it for him — 'it's a new apartment complex it's like less than a year old and maybe the address just hasn't updated in your system' — and there is no indication it was logged for anyone to fix.

No 'BOLDED details at the top of the email,' no 'reply with any corrections,' no 'any other questions before I let you go?' (she volunteered 'I think that answers all my questions'), and no hours or direct callback number — just 'give us a call back.'
Customer's name never used once in nine minutes. He asked for it twice and then never said 'Michelle.'
Day-of-week rate tiers never mentioned, even though the flexibility question was already on the table and the date moved from a Wednesday to a Thursday.
top_strength: Jules turned a frustrated website failure into a calm, competent quoting conversation, and his fee transparency was genuinely excellent. He recovered the broken address lookup without making it the customer's problem — 'Oh, no. That's okay. I can just use the zip code' — and then delivered the no-hidden-fees pitch better than most: 'The best part about this is we do not have any additional [fees], you know, we don't have anything like a fuel fee, no disassemble reassembly fees, no hidden fees at all. It's just straightforward the hour rate.' The customer bought it completely and played it back in her own words, comparing Einstein to competitors who quote '$130 an hour, then you also have these additional trip fees and check fees and fuel fees,' and Jules closed the loop cleanly: 'Exactly, that we do not have any extra fees like that... so you can easily calculate how much that would cost.' He also volunteered the no-deposit answer with real clarity ('we do not require any deposit. You only pay directly to the movers after everything is completed'), gave a dollarized range rather than a vague hourly ($505 at the minimum, $808 at four hours), covered the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute prorating, and sense-checked it with 'Does that make sense so far?' Stairs and floors were probed properly at both ends, and there was real human warmth in the exchange — the self-aware 'we're fully, I mean, we're fully available on the eighth. That's a weird way to say that' and the stairs banter left a customer who called in annoyed saying 'Okay, perfect. Thank you so much.'
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix, and it is not subtle: ask for the booking. Jules confirmed availability, quoted the price, answered the deposit objection before she raised it, and heard 'that makes sense' — and then said 'when you're ready to get this scheduled feel free to give us a call back.' The line he needed was, 'Michelle, since there's no deposit and nothing to lose, let me go ahead and hold Thursday the 8th for you right now — if you and your husband decide against it this weekend, you just reply to my email and I release it, no charge either way.' A no-deposit business has no reason to ever end a call on 'call us back.' Second priority: he heard the two biggest revenue and accuracy signals on the call and let both pass. She said 'I still have a lot of craft to pack' — that is 'Would you like us to handle the packing? It's the same $202 hourly rate plus materials, and one crew packing takes hours off what you'd spend doing it yourself' — and she asked him directly for a box benchmark and got 'No problem at all.' Third, and this is the estimate-accuracy issue Cameron is tracking: he collected third-floor-no-elevator at the origin, 30-plus boxes and climbing, and a Forney-to-Garland drive, and then quoted a range starting at the 2.5-hour minimum. Two movers cannot carry a one-bedroom load down three flights of stairs, drive it, and take it up to a third floor in 150 minutes. He should have said, 'Because we're carrying down three flights with no elevator on your end, I'd plan on five to six hours for two movers rather than the minimum — I'd rather over-prepare you than surprise you,' and then used it as the Save Your Ass opening: 'Here's how you cut that number — every box that's already sealed and stacked by the front door, every drawer emptied, everything small in your own car, comes straight off the clock.' Business items to close today: (1) the destination address 5620 Prosperity Drive in Garland still is not in the system and no zip was captured, so this record cannot be booked as it stands and the web-form defect the customer diagnosed for us is still live for every other lead at that complex — get it escalated to IT. (2) Her email was taken as 'JM Dody 01 @gmail.com' on a call where her last name (Doughty) was misheard twice and never spelled back; verify it before the estimate goes out or the entire follow-up is lost. (3) He told a customer whose lease starts October 7th that we have 'monthly training for the movers' that day and never directly answered her question 'Are you guys full on that day?' — she moved her own move rather than us finding a crew. Worth checking whether the 10/7 training day is a hard company-wide blackout, and if it is, reps need language for it that does not read as us being unavailable on a lease-start date.
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth and a couple of genuinely human moments — 'Oh, no,' 'No problem at all,' the self-deprecating 'that's a weird way to say that,' and a customer who arrived frustrated and left saying 'perfect, thank you so much' — but he never once used her name, and the delivery is dotted with restarts and half-finished sentences ('can you give me the address, removing everything through?', 'Might as well okay. Well, oh, gosh.') that keep it from reading as polished.
audio_review_reason: Several stretches of Jules's speech are incoherent in transcript ('we don't have any additional he's', 'so the cost of that would go anywhere awesome', 'and I met her, I would too'), and he asked 'Can I have your first and last name?' twice back to back — it cannot be determined from text whether this is ASR failure on a poor line or genuine mumbling and rushed pace, which is the difference between no coaching item and a clarity coaching item.
